text:
incident-bot: [PAGE] p99 latency SLO breach detected for tenant Wavecrest in us-west-2 — streaming responses showing stalls. Metrics: p95 480ms -> 1.2s, p99 1.1s -> 5.8s; streaming stall rate ↑ x12
maya: On-call here. Got the page, joining.
ryan: I'm pulling traces and pool metrics now. Is this single-tenant?
maya: Yes, Wavecrest is single-tenant on dedicated pool `dedicated-c-03`. We're seeing a big concurrency burst tied to a new prompt pattern they shipped.
emily: Metrics: token throughput for dedicated-c-03 dropped ~45%. KV cache miss rate spiked 9x. Logs show repeated long-prefix assembly ops.
tilly: Can we route Wavecrest to a different pool or enable a fallback? We should avoid mass restarts if possible.
emily: There is an immediate routing option: `route.override=dedicated-c-02` — we can flip with `rb service set-route wavecrest --pool=dedicated-c-02`, but need to check capacity in c-02.
ryan: Traces show a lot of sessions stuck in the streaming hotpath waiting for next token — partial responses buffered. Stack traces contain repeated `kvCache::miss()` frames. Suspect a prompt pattern that forces full KV recompute per token.
maya: Immediate mitigation: apply temporary tenant QPS throttle to protect the pool and reduce new inflight sessions. I'll apply `tenant_qps_limit=40` for Wavecrest.
incident-bot: Action started: set tenant_qps_limit for Wavecrest -> 40 (applied by maya).
maya: Throttle applied. Observing fewer new inflight sessions but active streams still stuck.
emily: We can also enable aggressive KV prefetch for repeated prefixes — there's a toggle `kvcache.prefetch=true` that helps long-prefix reuse.
ryan: Enabling prefetch for Wavecrest on dedicated-c-03 now: `rb feature toggle kvcache.prefetch --tenant=wavecrest --enable`
command-output: ```ok: toggled kvcache.prefetch for tenant wavecrest on dedicated-c-03
status: prefetch-ingestion started
```
maya: p95 has already moved from ~480ms to ~320ms; p99 trending down from 5.8s toward 1.6s within 60s of toggles.
emily: We also see pool memory pressure from in-memory prefix tables. I'll bump cache entries on the pool temporarily: `pool.dedicated-c-03.cache.max_entries 200k -> 400k`. This requires a rolling restart.
deploy-bot: Queued config change: bump `pool.dedicated-c-03.cache.max_entries` to 400000. Rolling restart scheduled one node at a time.
ryan: Rolling restart started — doing one node at a time to avoid mass disruption. Monitoring token throughput.
maya: Wavecrest engineering replied in their support thread: they shipped an embedding-aggregation that repeats a 32k delimiter across many prompts — that's the long-prefix source. They plan a client-side fix in ~45m to reduce prefix repetition.
emily: Good to know. With the throttle + prefetch + cache bump we've cut streaming stall frequency by ~86% from peak. p99 currently ~950ms and falling.
ryan: If memory/gc gets worse we'll failover routing for new sessions to dedicated-c-02 automatically when pool mem > 80%. I've pushed an alert to the autoswitch runbook.
maya: Summarizing live mitigations: 1) tenant QPS throttle applied, 2) kvcache.prefetch enabled for tenant, 3) pool cache size increased + rolling restart, 4) conditional routing to fallback pool if mem > 80%, 5) customer asked to fix prompt.
emily: Logs snippet showing KV miss signature and stall timestamps:```[2026-03-15T03:40:12Z] pool=dedicated-c-03 tenant=wavecrest request_id=abc123 STALL kvCache::miss keylen=32768 duration=4123ms```
maya: I'll hand off to ryan for follow-up in 30m once stable. Action items for post-incident: - add tenant-specific rate-limit baseline in prod templates - add automated fallback threshold for pool memory - customer outreach on prompt best-practices - backfill runbook entry for kvcache prefetch behavior.
ryan: I'll own the postmortem and playbook updates. Also proposing a permanent tenant qps cap with a staged ramp to avoid regressions.
incident-bot: Postmortem record created: https://redwood-internal/incident/5098765432 (private)
maya: Thanks team — I'll close the page once p99 stays <1s for 20m continuous.
incident-bot: Incident status -> monitoring/stable. last_update: 320s after initial page.
